facts.text: AMD will build a heterogeneous AI cluster in Seoul next spring that combines its own CPUs and GPUs with Korean AI chips.

articles.title: OpenAI employees flagged weak internal security before ChatGPT
"오픈AI, 수년간 내부 보안 취약점 경고 무시"...개발 속도 우선에 기밀 유출 위험

facts.text: OpenAI employees repeatedly warned the company's leadership and board about weaknesses in its security practices over several years, including before ChatGPT launched in late 2022, Reuters reported, citing five people familiar with the matter.
Some employees came away with the impression that executives were more concerned with keeping pace with rivals Google and Anthropic than addressing security risks.
OpenAI stored most of its code in a single repository (a monorepo), so anyone with access could potentially inspect nonpublic projects, the five sources said.
Three sources said OpenAI failed to carry out regular security checks on internal tools, including the sandboxes researchers use to test new models.
OpenAI disputed parts of the account: its most sensitive work is kept in separate, restricted repositories and the monorepo does not contain its model weights.
OpenAI said internal tools now undergo regular security checks under security chief Dane Stuckey, who joined in October 2024.
In August, product chief Thibault Sottiaux reassigned a quarter of OpenAI's production engineers to security work, one source said.
In October OpenAI said it had found a hidden recording device in a room used by senior executives; prosecutors charged former engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan with planting it.

stories.note: Reuters original 403; TNW and AI Times readable. Story broke Nov 3 (Reuters); outlets above are post-cutoff. Related: OpenAI hired Dan Driscoll (morning candidate), OpenAI security-sprint blog.

stories.title: Anthropic releases FlashProve, open-source way to prove which AI model wrote an output

articles.title: Anthropic is working on a system to prove AI models' identity
Progress on provable inference for large language models

facts.text: Anthropic is working on an open source system to verify which AI model produced a given output, according to a blog post published Tuesday.
The system, called FlashProve, is built to provide ... 'provable inference' — a cryptographic proof ... that a given output came from a specific model.
[It] could be used to prevent an AI company from secretly swapping in a cheaper model to cut costs, or a more expensive model to inflate its performance results.
the fingerprints don't reveal a model's weights, the internal numbers that define how it behaves and which closed-model makers like Anthropic and OpenAI keep private.
Research in the system is ongoing, and there are no plans to deploy it at Anthropic or any other lab.

For a large model (Llama 4 Maverick, 400B-parameter mixture of experts), a single H100 GPU generates proofs at around 110 tokens/second, with a proof size of ~19 MB per 1,024-token request ... This is ~70-95x the GPU time of running the model itself on vLLM.
We release our code, Lean proofs, and documentation under the Apache 2.0 license.
Claude found novel ways to apply state-of-the-art tools in the cryptography and security literature.

facts.text: The UK's Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA) will test servers that use light to run AI models, in a lab it funds, Oxford startup Lumai said on Tuesday.
The Scaling Inference Lab, backed by £50M from ARIA and run by the nonprofit CommonAI, will install Lumai's Iris servers as its first optical computing platform.
Lumai, spun out of Oxford University in 2021, encodes data into beams of light.
The company aims its hardware at 'prefill', the stage where a model first reads a user's prompt. Ordinary chips would still produce the answer.
Lumai claims its approach could cut data centre power use by up to 90%. It also says the system is at least 16 times more energy efficient per request than silicon alone.
None of these figures has been independently checked, and testing them is the lab's job.
Salience Labs, which also builds on Oxford research, raised $125M last month for optical switches.

articles.title: "AI가 다른 AI의 가중치 직접 수정"…재학습 없이 수학 평가 점수 6배 상승

facts.text: MIT 연구진은 2일(현지시간) AI가 신경망의 가중치를 직접 분석하고 수정하는 '가중치공간 프로그래밍(Weight-Space Programming)' 연구 결과를 공개했다. 벤처비트는 이를 신경망의 '유전자 편집'에 비유했다.
연구진은 오픈AI의 'GPT-6 아스트라'에 알리바바의 소형 모델 '큐원3.5-0.8B'의 수학 성능을 개선하라는 목표를 제시했다.
아스트라는 ... 15번째와 19번째 계층의 가중치 13만1072개를 수정했다. 이는 전체 약 8억개 가중치의 0.016%에 불과하다.
'MATH-500' 점수는 기존 7.9%에서 48.1%로 약 6.1배 높아졌다. 'GSM8K'도 13.8%에서 67.1%로, 'IFEval'도 21.0%에서 62.3%로 개선됐다.
수학적 추론 능력 자체가 6배 높아졌다는 의미는 아니다. ... MATH-500에서 출력 한도에 도달한 비율은 수정 전 93%에서 수정 후 33.1%로 낮아졌다.
구글의 소형 모델 '젬마 3 270M'에서도 수학 성능 개선을 시도했지만, 뚜렷한 성과를 얻지 못했다.
기존 미세조정보다 시간이나 비용이 적게 든다는 사실도 입증하지 못했으며, AI가 스스로의 성능을 지속적으로 높이는 자율적 자기 개선 능력까지 보여준 것은 아니라는 평이다.

articles.title: OpenAI hires former US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll for security role

facts.text: OpenAI has hired Dan Driscoll, the 26th Secretary of the US Army, the company said on Monday. He takes a new role: senior counselor for national security modernization.
His main focus is helping US allies use the technology responsibly.
Driscoll left the Pentagon in September after months of tension with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
As Army secretary, he oversaw nearly one million soldiers and more than 265,000 Army civilians, OpenAI said.
OpenAI said the hire builds on Daybreak, its cyber resilience programme with allies and partners.
In February, OpenAI agreed to deploy its models on the Defense Department's classified network. ... Anthropic is still fighting its Pentagon case in court.

stories.title: Palantir Q3: revenue +96% to $2.31B, but enterprise deals are short trials

articles.title: Hiding inside Palantir's skyrocketing quarter is a foreboding signal

facts.text: Revenue grew 96% from a year earlier, and 20% from the previous quarter, to $2.31 billion, beating analysts' expectations of $2.18 billion. It was the first time Palantir has topped $2 billion in a quarter.

Palantir's U.S. commercial revenue surpassed U.S. government revenue for the first time ever. The company reported $984 million in commercial contracts (up 148% from the year-ago quarter), versus $953 million in U.S. government revenue.
Enterprises are often signing short-term trials.
CEO Alex Karp: 'much quicker interaction, much quicker to deployment, shorter duration of the contract but then an ability to expand that contract dramatically'.
While the company closed a hefty $1.46 billion of total contract value from U.S. enterprises in the quarter, that's actually a decline from the record $2.13 billion in the previous quarter.
They increased guidance for U.S. commercial revenue to be 'in excess of $3.559 billion, representing a growth rate of at least 143%.'

stories.title: Apple restricts dating apps and AI companions to users 18 and up

articles.title: Apple restricts dating apps and AI companions to users 18 and up

facts.text: Apple is adjusting its App Store policies to make it more difficult for minors to use online dating apps or AI companions that engage in 'sexual or romantic content,' the tech giant shared in an announcement to developers on Monday.
Apple's new policy will require all apps offering dating or romantic relationship features to carry an 18+ rating.
Starting November 16, developers will be required to include new content descriptors to ensure their app's age ratings reflect its features.
As of last summer, top AI companion apps across the Apple App Store and Google Play had been downloaded 220 million times globally.
